lessons.title: যদি … তাহলে … (jôdi … tāhôle …) — if, then
lessons.gloss: if … then … — a real condition and what follows from it

segments.text: Say "for two years". (dui bôchhôr dhôre.) Then যদি, "if", and তাহলে, "then, in that case": both of which you know.

blocks.title: You'll want to know: if, then

segments.text: যদি কাল ঝড় হয়, তাহলে আমরা যাব না। jôdi kāl jhôṛ hôy, tāhôle āmrā jābô nā. — "If there's a storm tomorrow, we won't go."

The যদি half takes the present, even about tomorrow: হয়, not হবে. The তাহলে half takes the future. তাহলে may be left out: যদি তুমি আসো, আমি রান্না করব (jôdi tumi āso, āmi rānnā kôrbô), "if you come, I'll cook".

blocks.title: You'll want to know: if not

segments.text: Inside a যদি half, না comes before the verb, not after it:
যদি ট্রেন সময়মতো না আসে, তাহলে আমি বাসে যাব। jôdi ṭren sômôymôto nā āse, tāhôle āmi bāse jābô. — "If the train doesn't come on time, I'll take the bus."

lessons.title: বৃষ্টি হলে … (brishṭi hôle …) — the -le form, and otherwise
lessons.gloss: if it rains … — the -le form, and নাহলে, otherwise

segments.text: Say "If there's a storm tomorrow, we won't go". (jôdi kāl jhôṛ hôy, tāhôle āmrā jābô nā.) Then নাহলে, "otherwise".

blocks.title: You'll want to know: the -le form

segments.text: Bengali can say "if" with no যদি: the verb takes -লে, on the stem of the past, and stays the same for every person.
বৃষ্টি হলে আমরা বাড়িতে থাকব। brishṭi hôle āmrā bāṛite thākbô. — "If it rains, we'll stay at home."
বৃষ্টি (brishṭi) is "rain", and বৃষ্টি হওয়া is "to rain": "rain happens".

হওয়া becomes হলে, আসা becomes এলে, যাওয়া becomes গেলে, খাওয়া becomes খেলে, করা becomes করলে, কেনা becomes কিনলে: তুমি এলে আমি খুশি হব (tumi ele āmi khushi hôbô), "if you come, I'll be happy". The person is in the noun before it, never in the ending.
নাহলে, "otherwise", which you know, is না with this same হলে: "if it is not so".
তাড়াতাড়ি যেতে হবে, নাহলে ট্রেন ছেড়ে যাবে। tāṛātāṛi jete hôbe, nāhôle ṭren chheṛe jābe. — "We have to go quickly, otherwise the train will leave."

segments.text: আসা in the -লে form? (এলে.) Does -লে change for the person? (No.) "Otherwise"? (নাহলে: "if not so".)
Before the new one: say "If you come, I'll be happy". (tumi ele āmi khushi hôbô.)
ঢোকা — ḍhokā — "to enter, to go in".
বাড়িতে ঢুকে আমি জুতো খুললাম। bāṛite ḍhuke āmi juto khullām. — "I came into the house and took my shoes off."

The place you enter takes -এ or -তে: বাড়িতে, দোকানে. The ও of ঢোকা (ḍhokā) rises to উ in the past, the -e form and the -লে form, as খোলা does: সে দোকানে ঢুকল (she dokāne ḍhuklô), "she went into the shop"; ঢুকে; ঢুকলে.
ঢোকা (ḍhokā) is listed in CDIAL, as ḍhukā, "to enter", under a reconstructed ḍhukyati, "approaches" (CDIAL 5592): a form no text records, hence the star.

lessons.title: ঢ (ḍhô) — the letter at the start of ঢোকা (ḍhokā)
lessons.gloss: the letter ঢ — ḍhô, the letter at the start of ঢোকা

needs: a pen and something to write on
your eyes, for letter shapes on the page
your eyes, because the lesson points at something written down
your eyes or your hands for the steps that ask you to read, point, write or gesture
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on, your eyes, for letter shapes on the page, your eyes, because the lesson points at something written down and your eyes or your hands for the steps that ask you to read, point, write or gesture. You can listen to everything else now. I will say so again when we reach them, but leave these sections until you have stopped: Warm-up, Script you'll notice: ঢ, Guided Practice and Wrap-up Recall.

segments.text: Before the new one: say ঢোকা (ḍhokā), "to enter". Then read ট (ṭô) and ড (ḍô).
ঢ — ḍhô: the ড sound with a breath after it, as ঠ is ট with a breath. It opens ঢোকা (ḍhokā).

In the print of this book, ঢ (ḍhô) is ট without its raised hook. It has a headline; a straight stem stands under the left part of it; the stem's foot rounds into a bowl, and the bowl's right side ends in a solid knob, tucked inside the curve under the right half of the headline. The right side does not reach the headline. Look at ট beside it: below the headline the two are alike, and ট has the hook above.

blocks.title: Writing: ঢ — copy the printed shape

segments.text: Put your pen beside ঢ (ḍhô) and copy the shape you can see, slowly and large. Check the copy against the print: the headline, the stem on the left, the round bottom, the solid knob, and the gap between the knob and the headline.

This book does not yet tell you where to start ঢ (ḍhô) or which way the pen goes. That is not written down here until it can be written down with a source. Copying the printed shape needs no such source, and it is how the shape becomes yours in the meantime.

segments.text: Which letter opens ঢোকা (ḍhokā)? (ঢ (ḍhô).) What does its right side end in? (A solid knob.) What does ট have that ঢ (ḍhô) does not? (The hook above the headline.)

feedback.incorrect: Reopen ঢ beside ট: same body, no hook above. Then write ঢোকা again.
